reviewer: Codex with one fresh GPT-6.1-Sol medium reviewer; quantifier clarification applied and passed on follow-up

claims.summary: For fixed binary old inputs of degree<=delta in a Boolean PC pseudoideal J_D, original accuracy h, coefficient bound T>=1 and common binary coefficient basis, suppose degree<=b weights W_j have successful maps with row spaces R_j. If k=dim(sum R_j)<=h and b+TB<=D for B>=max(2,h(delta+1)+delta), a padded basis of the union is one map successful at every W_j and their binary linear combinations. Row reduction, extending bases by factors and paid row invariance retain original h and B; number of witnesses does not enter the degree. No survival, union-dimension bound, or source-wide varying-weight reconstruction is asserted.
claims.assessment: Working paid composition of the row-gauge lemma, passed by one fresh medium reviewer with adaptive-versus-uniform scope clarified.
claims.rationale: Tests whether several weight witnesses can share a normalizer without paying a separate full row budget for each.
claims.next_action: Bound the needed row-space union or use adaptive choices; do not assume this sufficient common-map condition is necessary.

claims.summary: For all h,T>=1, r=h(T+1)+1 independent Boolean input bits, accuracy h, all binary coefficient maps of degree<=T (also allowing additional old bits), and Boolean-only J_D with D>=1+T(2h+1): every homogeneous linear weight has an adaptive successful map but no single permitted map serves that whole linear space; moreover x_1 and 1+x_1 are feasible surviving weights while their sum 1 is infeasible. The complement weight uses h packed groups of T+1 inputs; unit-weight failure follows from forced degree-r zero-test versus product degree<=r-1. Weighted field certificates fit. This is a consistent Boolean-cube control, not a charged hard-quotient obstruction.
claims.assessment: Working all-parameter adaptive-weight control passed by one fresh medium reviewer; uses existing packing and the pointwise degree barrier, retaining the full degree-bounded coefficient domain and Boolean-only scope.
claims.rationale: Separates adaptive feasibility from uniform maps and refutes treating arbitrary feasible-weight sets as linear spaces.
claims.next_action: Any linear common-weight construction must justify a source/quotient-specific subset or additional structure; no unrestricted lower bound follows from this control.

relationships: Row-reduces each map and transports an extended union basis to one common basis at the original paid ceiling.
Reuses its group telescoping and degree barrier with one additional input and complementary weights; the new conclusions concern adaptive feasibility and nonlinearity.
Shows its uniform-map union-rank budget is sufficient rather than necessary for adaptive feasibility of every weight in a linear space.
